title: Cheaper Mobile Internet Reaches a Milestone — But the Digital Divide Remains
title_zh: 移动互联网价格首次达标，但数字鸿沟依然巨大
source_name: UN News — “World News in Brief” 3 Nov 2026 (ITU affordability milestone); ITU Facts and Figures 2026
summary_zh: 国际电信联盟（ITU）《事实与数字 2026》显示：全球约 63 亿人上网，占世界人口的 76%；内陆发展中国家（LLDCs）和小岛屿发展中国家（SIDS）的基础移动数据包中位价格首次降至人均国民总收入的 2% 目标以下。但最不发达国家仍高达 6.1%，高收入与低收入国家在 5G 覆盖和月均流量上差距悬殊。本文适合积累数字鸿沟、可负担性与国际发展类雅思词汇。
paragraphs: For the first time, mobile internet has become affordable in the world’s landlocked developing countries (LLDCs) and small island developing States (SIDS). According to the International Telecommunication Union’s Facts and Figures 2026, the median price of a basic mobile data plan in both groups has fallen below the internationally agreed target of 2 per cent of average income, or GNI per capita.

The shift is clearest in the numbers. In LLDCs, the median price dropped from 2.7 per cent to 1.7 per cent of income. In SIDS, it eased from 2.1 per cent to 1.9 per cent. Globally, some 6.3 billion people — 76 per cent of the world’s population — are online this year, up from 6.1 billion, or about 74 per cent, in 2025. Roughly two billion people remain unconnected.

Progress is uneven. In the least developed countries (LDCs), prices stay stubbornly high at 6.1 per cent of income, only slightly down from 6.3 per cent. Three in ten economies still meet neither the mobile nor the fixed broadband affordability target. Cheaper plans in some regions have not closed the wider gap.

Connection quality widens the divide further. 5G networks reach 86 per cent of people in high-income countries but only 4 per cent in low-income ones. In low-income countries, the average mobile user consumes about 3.4 GB of data a month — around six times less than in richer nations. Being online does not always mean having fast, useful access.

ITU Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin warned that in the age of AI, being offline means being shut out of opportunities from education to employment. She urged governments and partners to expand meaningful connectivity so that lower prices turn into real chances to learn, work and take part in society.

For IELTS learners, this report links technology, inequality and development. Notice how it contrasts groups that have met an affordability target with those that have not, and how it moves from price data to quality and opportunity. Similar compare–contrast and cause–effect patterns often appear in Reading passages and in Writing Task 2 essays on digital access and global development.
paragraphs_zh: 移动互联网首次在全球内陆发展中国家（LLDCs）和小岛屿发展中国家（SIDS）变得可负担。据国际电信联盟（ITU）《事实与数字 2026》，这两类国家基础移动数据包的中位价格，已降至国际公认目标——平均收入（或人均国民总收入）的 2%——以下。
变化在数字上最为清晰。在内陆发展中国家，中位价格从占收入的 2.7% 降至 1.7%；在小岛屿发展中国家，则从 2.1% 缓降至 1.9%。全球层面，今年约有 63 亿人上网，占世界人口的 76%，高于 2025 年的 61 亿人（约 74%）。仍有大约 20 亿人尚未联网。
进展并不均衡。在最不发达国家（LDCs），价格仍顽固地高达收入的 6.1%，仅略低于原先的 6.3%。仍有十分之三的经济体既未达到移动宽带、也未达到固定宽带的可负担性目标。部分地区套餐更便宜，并未能弥合更广泛的差距。
连接质量进一步拉大鸿沟。5G 网络覆盖高收入国家 86% 的人口，但在低收入国家仅覆盖 4%。在低收入国家，移动用户平均每月使用约 3.4 GB 流量——大约只有较富裕国家的六分之一。上网并不总意味着拥有快速、有用的接入。
ITU 秘书长多琳·博格丹-马丁警告说，在人工智能时代，离线意味着被教育到就业等机会拒之门外。她敦促各国政府与合作伙伴扩大「有意义的连接」，使更低的价格真正转化为学习、工作和参与社会的机会。
对雅思学习者来说，这篇报道把技术、不平等与发展联系在一起。注意它如何对比已达到可负担性目标的群体与尚未达标的群体，又如何从价格数据转向质量与机会。类似的「对比」和「因果」展开方式，常出现在阅读文章以及数字接入与全球发展类写作任务二中。

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Mobile internet is now free in every country.
LLDCs and SIDS have met the mobile-internet affordability target for the first time, but large digital divides remain.
5G already covers most people in low-income countries.
The ITU wants to stop publishing Facts and Figures reports.
questions.explanation: 主旨：内陆发展中国家和小岛屿发展中国家首次达到移动互联网可负担性目标，但数字鸿沟（价格、质量、流量）依然很大。

evidence.quote: For the first time, mobile internet has become affordable in the world’s landlocked developing countries (LLDCs) and small island developing States (SIDS).

questions.prompt: What share of income does a basic mobile data plan still cost in the least developed countries?
questions.explanation: 最不发达国家的基础移动数据包价格仍占收入的 6.1%（此前为 6.3%）。

evidence.quote: prices stay stubbornly high at 6.1 per cent of income

questions.prompt: Why does the ITU Secretary-General say expanding meaningful connectivity matters in the age of AI?
options: Because being offline means being shut out of opportunities from education to employment.
Because AI has already made mobile data free everywhere.
Because high-income countries no longer need 5G.
Because two billion people have already gone offline this year.
questions.explanation: 秘书长指出：在人工智能时代，离线意味着被教育到就业等诸多机会拒之门外，因此需要扩大有意义的连接。

evidence.quote: being offline means being shut out of opportunities from education to employment
